verdict.rationale: Phaser's core game framework is code-first, and the Phaser Game Agent MCP server explicitly exposes '40+ specialised tools' letting AI agents perform scene editing, particle emitters, filters, and layer reorganization tasks that mirror the visual Scene Editor's drag-and-drop UI, with agents callable from Claude Desktop, Cursor, GitHub Copilot etc. However this is a separate hosted product (not an installable open API/SDK), and the runtime probe confirms there's no @phaserjs MCP npm package — only a hosted 'Connect your coding agent' service — so parity is asserted but not independently verified feature-by-feature against every Editor capability (e.g. SFX/music generation, tilemap editors). Missing for 10: independent verification of full 1:1 parity between the 40+ MCP tools and every visual-editor feature, and an installable/open (non-hosted) API confirming AI-native equivalence.
